case_studies.title: Deployment-Time Memorization in Foundation-Model Agents
case_studies.abstract: Foundation-model agents are increasingly long-lived systems that remember users across interactions, making memorization an explicit deployment-time function rather than solely a property of model weights. Existing work addresses parametric memorization or audits fixed memory configurations, but does not characterize how memory-design choices jointly shape personalization utility, extraction risk, and deletion fidelity. We study this surface as deployment-time memorization, formulating agent memory as a privacy-utility frontier measured by Personalization Recall (PR) and Adversarial Extraction
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of balancing personalization and privacy in long-lived foundation-model agents by characterizing how memory-design choices impact these factors. The researchers built a framework to study deployment-time memorization, forming a privacy-utility frontier. The result shows how to measure personalization recall and adversarial extraction risk.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on artificial intelligence and model development rather than cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: This paper explores deployment-time memorization in foundation-model agents, which is relevant to the development and deployment of AI-powered systems. The concept of a privacy-utility frontier is novel and has implications for IT professionals working with AI. However, its direct relevance to IT infrastructure and deployment is limited, and the actionability of the results is moderate.

case_studies.title: Context-Fractured Decomposition Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents: Exploiting Artifact Provenance Gaps
case_studies.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents interact with the world through actions that persist state in artifacts (e.g., workspace files or logs). Consequently, jailbreak defenses must reason about cross-step composition rather than isolated text. Yet most existing attacks and defenses, including ``multi-turn'' jailbreaks such as Crescendo and Tree of Attacks,still assume a single contiguous conversation visible to the defender. This assumption breaks down in real agent pipelines, where enforcement is fragmented across tools, modules, and time, and where artifact provenance is often not tracked. We operationalize
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of exploiting gaps in artifact provenance in tool-using LLM agents, building a Context-Fractured Decomposition Attack to test defenses, and resulting in a better understanding of vulnerabilities in cross-step composition. The research built an attack to expose weaknesses in current jailbreak defenses. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: Multimodal large language models can write code to produce complex programs as well as use programs to do 3D modeling, which opens up a new avenue for 3D generation powered by their priors, world knowledge and reasoning. Yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate 3D modeling through code. Such modeling demands more than runnable code: from a text or visual specification, a model must generate a parametric 3D program that is geometrically precise, semantically aligned and assembly-consistent. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating multimodal large language models for 3D modeling through code, the authors built a benchmark called P3D-Bench, and the result is a more accurate way to generate parametric 3D programs. The benchmark tests a model's ability to produce geometrically precise, semantically aligned, and assembly-consistent 3D models. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Sim2Schedule: A Simulator-Guided LLM Framework for Autonomous Open-Pit Mine Scheduling
case_studies.abstract: Open-pit mine scheduling is a critical process for maximizing economic return under complex geotechnical and operational constraints. While Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) provides mathematically optimal baselines, its exponential computational complexity and inability to adapt in real time limit its practical deployment in dynamic industrial environments. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of open-pit mine scheduling by building a simulator-guided Large Language Model framework, resulting in a more adaptable and efficient scheduling process. The framework uses a custom simulator to guide the LLM in making autonomous decisions. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Learning What to Remember: Observability-Safe Memory Retention via Constrained Optimization for Long-Horizon Language Agents
case_studies.abstract: Long-horizon language agents accumulate observations, reasoning traces, and retrieved facts that exceed their finite context windows, making memory retention a fundamental resource-allocation problem. Existing memory systems improve management through heuristic scoring, retrieval optimization, or learned compression, but largely treat retention as a local decision problem and do not explicitly model its long-term consequences under realistic observability constraints. To fill this gap, we formulate memory retention as a constrained stochastic optimization problem with explicit budget feasibili
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of memory retention in long-horizon language agents by building a constrained optimization system, resulting in improved memory management. The system allows agents to retain relevant information while discarding unnecessary data. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Mind the Gap: Bridging Behavioral Silos with LLMs in Multi-Vertical Recommendations
case_studies.abstract: In multi-vertical e-commerce platforms like DoorDash, relatively newer product verticals such as grocery and retail present a significant opportunity for personalization innovation. A key challenge lies in solving the "cold start" problem for users. This paper introduces a novel framework for enhancing recommendation quality by transferring knowledge from data-rich verticals (e.g., restaurants at DoorDash) to data-sparse ones. We leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform generative inference, synthesizing sparse, high-dimensional features that encapsulate latent user affinities. Specifi
case_studies.summary: This research solves the 'cold start' problem in multi-vertical e-commerce platforms by transferring knowledge from data-rich areas to data-sparse ones, using a framework that leverages Large Language Models to generate user features. The result is improved recommendation quality for newer product verticals. This work is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
